previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease and chronic hepatitis C was admitted for her second cycle of adjuvant doxorubicin and cisplatin chemotherapy for high-grade osteosarcoma of the left tibia. She had previously experienced severe delayed nausea, dehydration, and syncope after cycle one, requiring hospitalization. This admission was elective and uncomplicated; she tolerated chemotherapy well with only mild nausea and a resolving dry cough. Her labs showed mild anemia, for which she received a red blood cell transfusion prior to discharge, and reactive thrombocytosis. Liver enzymes remained mildly elevated, attributed to chemotherapy, hepatitis C, and sickle cell disease, but hepatology approved continuation of treatment. She was discharged on scheduled antiemetics, including a dexamethasone taper, and instructions to begin Neupogen injections the following morning to mitigate neutropenia risk. Follow-up was arranged, with emphasis on hydration, infection monitoring, and adherence to anti-nausea regimen.

# Left tibia osteosarcoma: Completed cycle ___.  No hydroxyurea 
(on hold through cycle #6).  Treatment included doxorubicin 
25mg/m2 Days ___ and cisplatin 50mg/m2 continuous infusion Days 
___.  She tolerated chemo well with minimal nausea.  Scheduled 
and PRN anti-emetics.  Dexamethasone taper at discharge with 
scheduled ondansetron and promethazine.  Consider adding 
aprepitant.  G-CSF to start 24hr after chemo finishes (Neupogen 
instead of Neulasta for ability to titrate and to prevent 
leukemoid reaction and potential sickling).  Scheduled 
anti-emetics at discharge to prevent delayed nausea encountered 
with cycle #1.
.
# Sickle cell disease: Chronic hemolysis, functionally asplenic. 
 Got hydroxyurea x2d for leukocytosis post-Neulasta after cycle 
#1.  Continued folate.  Hold further hydroxyurea until completed 
with all chemo cycles.  Hydromorphone PRN.

negative.  AFP normal. EBV IgG positive, CMV IgG positive, 
indicating past infection.  No chemo dose reduction required 
unless bilirubin increases or transaminitis becomes severe.  
Plan to follow hep C viral load periodically.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital for cycle #3 
cisplatin/doxorubicin chemotherapy for osteosarcoma of the left 
leg.  You tolerated this well and will need to start G-CSF 
(Neupogen) injections 48 HOURS AFTER CHEMOTHERAPY FINISHED and 
continue this EVERY OTHER DAY in order to stimulate white blood 
cell production.  Despite this, your blood counts will likely 
become low making you susceptible to infections.  You should 
avoid crowds and sick contacts until the white blood cell count 
improves.  Prior to leaving the hospital, you were transfused 
one unit of red blood cells for severe anemia.
